title: Nuclear extraction from endometrial tumors for single nuclei sequencing
author: gracefoley
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b3vfqn3n
materials: Chop tissue using a scalpel until mostly homogenized

steps.title: Prepare Tissue and Buffer
steps.instruction: Place frozen endometrial tumor tissue in a well of a 6 well plate containing cold NST disassociation buffer, ensuring the plate is on ice.

substeps.instruction: Use 0.5 mL of buffer per 0.2 grams of endometrial tumor tissue
Use a total of 1 mL of cold NST disassociation buffer

steps.title: Incubate Tissue
steps.instruction: Incubate the solution on ice for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Filter Homogenized Solution
steps.instruction: Filter the homogenized solution through a 40 uM falcon cell strainer into a 50 mL falcon tube.

substeps.instruction: Use an additional 1 mL of NST buffer to rinse the well and filter

steps.title: First Nuclei Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the nuclei at 300 g for 10 minutes and aspirate the supernatant completely.

steps.title: Resuspend in ST Buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet and bring the total volume up to 5 mL using ST buffer.

steps.title: Second Nuclei Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Transfer the solution to a 15 mL conical tube and centrifuge for 10 minutes at 300 g at 4°C.

steps.title: Wash Nuclei Pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellets on ice in 1 mL of the ST buffer.

steps.title: Final Nuclei Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge nuclei at 300 g for 10 minutes and aspirate the supernatant completely.

steps.title: Final Resuspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the nuclei pellet in resuspension buffer to achieve a concentration of 1,000 nuclei per uL.

steps.title: Quality Control
steps.instruction: Examine nuclear membranes at 40x-60x magnification to ensure high nuclear membrane quality with minimal blebbing.
